title: Vitruvyan Motus trace document, v1
description: DRAFT v1 (post cross-review). A trace is a run header plus an ordered append-only sequence of records: the causal, replayable account of one run. Two canonical encodings of ONE logical model: (a) a single JSON document matching this schema's root; (b) JSONL — UTF-8, LF line endings, no BOM, exactly one header line matching #/$defs/TraceHeader followed by one line per record, each matching #/$defs/Record; blank/whitespace-only lines are tolerated and ignored (a crash may leave a trailing partial or empty line — tolerance is the honest reading). A JSON document and a JSONL stream are equivalent iff header (minus records) and record sequences are structurally equal; fixtures pin this. Integrity hashes, when activated (schema 1.1+), are computed over the canonical object form (contract/README.md), never over encoding bytes. Cross-record rules a conformant validator MUST enforce beyond this schema (the T-rules; the executable validator ships in contract/validate.py): (T1) seq is monotonic and gapless from 1; (T2) run_started appears EXACTLY ONCE, as the first record; (T3) the last record of a finished run is run_completed | run_failed | run_cancelled, and NOTHING follows a terminal record; a stream ending without a terminal record — including at EOF mid-line — is incomplete/crash-truncated and MUST be treated per guarantees.md invariant II; (T4) every read origin of kind transition references the seq of an EARLIER transition record, and its collection/index address an existing element of that record's writes; origins of kind initial address an existing element of run_started.initial_state; a header/metadata read's key must exist in run.metadata (a missing key is an `absent` read, not a header read); (T5) node, after, selected, candidates[].target, active_attempt.node and run_failed.failed_node name nodes declared in the fingerprinted GraphSpec, or the literal END where permitted; (T6) every transition record (node, attempt) is opened by the immediately preceding attempt_started with the same (node, attempt); an unclosed attempt_started may be followed only by run_cancelled (whose active_attempt names it), by run_failed with a non-node cause, or by EOF (incomplete); CONVERSELY, run_cancelled.active_attempt, when non-null, names exactly the immediately preceding unclosed attempt_started — when the preceding record is not an unclosed attempt_started, active_attempt is null; (T7) run_failed.failed_node is non-null iff cause.kind is node_failure, and cause.record_seq, when non-null, references an existing record; (T8) routing correlations: matched has exactly one taken candidate, whose condition is {kind: map, key == value} and whose target equals selected; default has exactly one taken candidate with condition kind default (and, when the spec is available, value absent from the map keys); static has exactly one candidate, taken, condition kind static, target equal to selected; miss has zero taken candidates and selected END; the candidate list contains every map entry of the spec's route step exactly once, plus the default entry when declared; for matched/default, written_at references an existing EARLIER transition whose committed writes.decisions contain the key `on`, and the R10-most-recent such value equals the routed value; (T9) every ts and created_ts is a CALENDAR-VALID RFC 3339 UTC instant — the pattern alone admits month 13, so the validator checks the date for real; (J1) values are strict RFC 8259: NaN/Infinity/-Infinity are refused by the validator and the CLI parser even where Python's json would accept them.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS trace schema. Single-sourced in the package; a contract test asserts equality.

TraceHeader.description: Line 1 of the JSONL encoding: this document minus records — so both encodings name the schema version that produced them.

run_id.description: Exposed as `.trace_id` on the legacy compatibility view (guarantees.md §4).

durability_profile.description: Which crash guarantee this run bought. See guarantees.md invariant II.

sink.description: Sink configuration disclosing the loss window. Validator rule H1: when durability_profile is `buffered`, `sink` MUST be present WITH BOTH disclosure keys (flush_interval_ms and chunk_records) — an empty sink object discloses nothing and does not satisfy the rule. Optional otherwise.

replay.description: The capability DECLARED at run start. The FINAL capability — after any mid-run downgrade (node-protocol.md §6.2) — is on the terminal record; when both exist, the terminal record is authoritative.

metadata.description: Run provenance. Open map; the keys below are the standard, tooling-expected vocabulary. Consumers MAY add their own keys (Terraveler's carta_version maps onto ruleset_version).

actor.description: Whose authority the run acts under.

causation_id.description: The event that woke this run.

correlation_id.description: The broader request this run belongs to.

ruleset_version.description: Which consumer-defined ruleset/constitution was in force. Domain-neutral name; what a consumer calls it (carta, policy, charter) is its business.

capability.description: Explicit, recorded property. Absence of a declaration never implies reproducibility; a run that did not declare it is `none`.

constraints.description: Machine-readable reasons for a non-full capability, e.g. 'node:fetch_page:ambient_time' or the standard reason 'undeclared'.

ReplayStatus.description: full carries no constraints; partial/none carry at least one motivating constraint ('undeclared' is the standard reason for runs that never declared reproducibility).

ts.description: From the run clock — never from ambient wall time (invariant IV.1).

payload_hash.description: Schema 1.0: ALWAYS null. Non-null hashes require schema 1.1+, which ships the algorithm, the chain validator and an unambiguous activation indicator — 1.0 refuses them so unverified hashes cannot masquerade as tamper evidence.

intent.description: The run's declared intent, if any. Readable by nodes; reads resolve as origin {kind: header, field: intent}.

initial_state.description: Snapshot of everything present before the first transition (all arrays may be empty). Reads with origin kind `initial` address into these arrays by collection and index — a seeded run is replayable and why-value-answerable for its seed.

AttemptStarted.description: Opens every attempt, before the node is invoked (T6). This is what makes a cancellation or crash mid-node EVIDENT instead of absent: an unclosed attempt_started names the node that was in flight, and effects it may or may not have caused are declared unknown — not erased from history.

node.description: Node name as declared in the GraphSpec (T5).

attempt.description: Matches the opening attempt_started (T6). Every attempt gets its own attempt_started + transition pair — retries are never hidden.

outcome.description: What the ATTEMPT did: returned a state, raised, or was cancelled cooperatively mid-checkpoint. Distinct from disposition — what the RUNNER then did about it.

disposition.description: The runner's policy decision: commit the returned state; retry the node (a new attempt_started follows); abort the run (run_failed follows, under strict); continue past the failure (exploration). Correlations are enforced by schema conditionals: returned→commit; raised→retry|abort|continue; cancelled→abort.

effect_class.description: The node's resolved class (declared in the GraphSpec or defaulted to external_effect). Recorded here so the trace document is self-sufficient for replay-mode selection. pure implies an empty effects list (schema-enforced).

key.description: The logical key read (fact/decision key, metadata key, or the collection name for scans). Captured, not declared.

reads.description: Every read the node actually performed, each with the structured origin of the exact value read — collection and index, not just a transition. Absent reads are captured too: reading a missing key can steer control flow as much as a present value.

effects.description: Per-effect descriptions (node-protocol.md §4). v1.0 records description only; receipts and reuse-on-replay are additive in schema 1.1 (Motus 0.6). For raised/cancelled attempts this list is best-effort: effects the runtime observed before the interruption.

context_draws.description: Every RunContext draw this attempt made, in draw order. Empty for nodes that drew nothing.

violations.description: Declared-vs-captured mismatches (node-protocol.md §3.2). Recorded in v1.0; enforcement is version-gated to 0.6.

error.description: Null iff outcome is returned or cancelled; the raising error otherwise (schema-enforced).

Writes.description: Everything this attempt appended. Transactional rule (node-protocol.md §7): writes exist only when the node returned and the runner committed — an attempt that raised or was cancelled has, by the state→state protocol, handed nothing to the runner, so its writes are structurally empty. What such a node did internally before raising never reached the run.

oneOf.description: The value read is records[seq].writes[collection][index] (T4). Collection + index make the edge per-VALUE: two same-key writes in one transition, or a fact and a decision sharing a key, resolve unambiguously.
The value read is the run's intent, or the metadata entry named by the read's key.

The node read the collection as a whole (iteration, len, search) rather than one addressed value. The read's key is the collection name. Coarse by nature: a scan depends on everything in the collection at that point.
The key was looked up and not found. A read-miss is causal evidence — it can steer control flow — so it is recorded, never dropped.

after.description: The node whose committed transition triggered this routing (T5).

on.description: The decision key routed on; null exactly for static steps (schema-enforced by outcome conditionals).

value.description: The observed decision value (Value admits JSON null — no duplicate null branch, per cross-review MF-02). String for matched/default (graphspec R9); anything, including null when the key was never decided, for miss; null for static (schema-enforced by the outcome conditionals).

written_at.description: seq of the transition whose committed write is the decision routed on (graphspec R10) — the routing record's own causal edge. Integer for matched/default; null for static and for a miss whose key was never decided.

outcome.description: matched: value hit a map key. default: value missed the map and the declared default was taken. miss: strict route missed (graphspec R7) — selected is END; the run then fails under policy strict and ends with the miss on record under exploration. static: a next/terminal step, no dispatch.

selected.description: A declared node name, or the literal string END.

condition.description: WHY this route was a candidate: the map key it answers to, the declared default, or the static next/terminal edge. Two map entries pointing at one target stay distinguishable.

candidates.description: Every route possible at this point — all map entries exactly once, the default once when declared, or the single static edge — taken and not taken (T8). This is what why-not answers are made of.

replay.description: FINAL replay capability after any mid-run downgrade. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

record_seq.description: The record that evidences the cause (the failing transition, the miss routing record), when one exists (T7).

cause.description: Structured cause so failure is explainable without parsing messages: a node raised, a strict route missed, the required sink refused the trace, a value failed boundary validation, the max_transitions safety limit tripped (transition_limit_exceeded), or the runner itself failed. PERSISTENCE LIMITATION (cross-review, OPEN-08): when the cause is sink_failure, THIS record's own persistence through the failed sink is best-effort — the run's logical failure toward the caller is still guaranteed (invariant II), but the persisted trace may end crash-truncated exactly as its durability profile describes. The contract cannot promise to write the death certificate into the register that just burned; it promises the death is declared.

failed_node.description: Non-null iff cause.kind is node_failure (T7). The accumulated trace up to and including this record survives — failure preservation is invariant-level.

replay.description: FINAL replay capability. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

reason.description: Cancellation is a first-class, trace-recorded runner outcome — never a silently abandoned generator.

active_attempt.description: The attempt in flight when cancellation landed, or null if cancellation fell between nodes. T6 binds BOTH directions: non-null active_attempt names exactly the immediately preceding UNCLOSED attempt_started; when the preceding record is not an unclosed attempt_started, active_attempt MUST be null — it can neither invent an attempt nor resurrect a closed one. Whether the in-flight attempt's external effects happened is UNKNOWN and recorded as such by this structure — the evidence is preserved, not erased.

replay.description: FINAL replay capability. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

source.description: Free-form provenance label supplied by the node. The kernel records it and never interprets it.

Fact.description: A RECORDED ASSERTION by a node — evidence of what was asserted, by whom, from what claimed source, at what point in the run. Never a claim of truth, verification, or endorsement: Fact/Decision/Rejection are neutral workflow primitives (guarantees.md invariant III note), and attributing truth to them is the consumer's business.

Decision.description: The Motus-native decision: a keyed, routable value with an optional reason. Distinct from the legacy Axis Decision(description, timestamp), which never enters a v1 trace — see guarantees.md §4 for the compatibility strategy.

Rejection.description: A recorded not-taken: what was declined and why. `evidence` is optional; when present it is a Value (which itself admits JSON null).

class.description: The class of THIS effect. `pure` is a node-level classification (Transition.effect_class), not an effect — a pure effect is an oxymoron and does not validate.

idempotency_key.description: Required for external_effect once effect enforcement lands (0.7); optional and recorded-only in v1.0.

oneOf.description: Any RFC 8259 JSON value EXCEPT an object claiming the reserved top-level discriminator kind: 'redacted' — such an object must be a well-formed RedactedValue or it is invalid everywhere. This keeps redacted values reserved and runtime-produced within a trace (they are not cryptographically unforgeable; a trace received from outside is only as trustworthy as its provenance until integrity activates in 1.1).

RedactedValue.description: Invariant V: structural completeness without content exposure. The hash and policy reference are evidence; the secret is not. Produced only by the runtime's redaction API (node-protocol.md §5).

Json.description: An RFC 8259 JSON value, strictly: object keys are strings; NaN and Infinity are refused at the write boundary (Python's json module accepts them by default — Motus does not); values round-trip structurally. A value that cannot be written down under these rules is a contract violation at the boundary, not a silent pass-through.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC with the literal Z suffix — the single canonical emission (readers MAY accept +00:00 in legacy inputs; writers emit Z only). From the run clock (invariant IV.1).

Fingerprint.description: Kind-prefixed SHA-256 over canonical form. See contract/README.md.
